title: Responsive video embed
when: The user wants a video on a page, either a local file or an embed from a video host, sized for every screen.
prompt:
Goal: A video that keeps its aspect ratio, loads light, has captions and never autoplays with sound.
Steps:
1. Wrap it in a box with aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 and make the iframe or video width: 100%; height: 100%.
2. Local file: <video controls preload="metadata" playsinline poster width height> with <source type="video/mp4"> and <track kind="captions" srclang label default>.
3. Embed: the iframe has a title naming the video, loading="lazy", allowfullscreen and the host privacy enhanced domain when one exists.
4. Facade for embeds: a poster img and <button type="button" aria-label="Play video: title">; on click create the iframe with createElement.
5. Decorative loops: autoplay muted loop with a Pause button, and no autoplay under prefers-reduced-motion.
Quality bar:
- A transcript or summary link sits under the video.
- The poster shows what the video is.
- No layout shift while loading.
Pitfalls:
- Fixed width and height that overflow phones.
- An iframe with no title.
- Autoplay with sound.
Verify:
- [ ] The wrapper keeps the ratio at 375 px.
- [ ] The iframe or video has a title or captions track.
- [ ] The poster image has alt.
- [ ] The facade button has a name.
Output: The video block in the page, video.css and video.js for the facade.

examples.output: aspect-ratio 16/9 box, poster with Play video button that creates the iframe with a title, transcript link
